rows.41:97f4:
Then Sato came to visit her.
"Hirai, why were you absent today?"
"..."
She couldn't say a thing.
"...I'm sorry.
I said too much yesterday, too."
"..."
"Um, who is this person you like?"
"..."
Without a word, she took Sato's hand.
Sato looked a little surprised, and then he squeezed her hand back.{p}
rows.41:9970:
...After that, the two of them started going out.
Whether that was because of Hirai's black magic, I'll leave to your imagination, {a}.
A few years after they graduated, Hirai and Sato got married.
But...{p}
rows.41:9a40:
On the day of the wedding, Hirai suddenly disappeared, they say.
The ceremony was held at a hotel in Tokyo, apparently.
She left the hall for her outfit change, to put on a white wedding dress, and after that...
at some point, she was just gone.
Everyone searched for her in a panic.
And then...{p}
rows.41:9ce8: "I meant to settle for two or three drops, but it was so delicious that I savored every last one..."{p}
rows.41:9da8:
That's the end of my story, but...
The seventh one still isn't here, huh.
What should we do now?
Hey, {a}...?{p}
rows.41:9e28:
Her eyes suddenly fell on her pet cat.
After all, it was only two or three drops of blood.
She decided she'd just get it from her own cat.
First, she let the cat sniff some catnip.{p}
rows.41:9ed8: Then, once the cat was in a daze, she put the box cutter's blade to it.{p}
rows.41:9f28:
"Mrrryaaaaagh!☆"
The cat's eyes bulged, and it fought back with its claws out.
She had only meant to make a little cut, but it reacted awfully violently.
Even though she'd given it catnip.
She jumped back in surprise.
And the cat ran away.{p}
rows.41:a0dc:
...It was a quiet night.
Inside the magic circle lay the bloodstained carpet fibers.
Somehow, she couldn't sit still.
She'd tried the black magic, all right, but now she was getting anxious.
She was starting to scare herself.
I want to see Sato.
That was what she thought.
It wasn't so much to test the black magic's power; she just wanted to see him so badly she couldn't stand it.
So she phoned Sato and called him out.
To the school, at night.
When she called him, Sato hurried over to the school gate.{p}
rows.41:a29c:
She was standing there all alone.
Looking like she was about to cry.
She looked so sad that Sato was a little thrown.
"Sato..."
Hirai was the first to speak.
"Sato, I love you..."
She said it, biting her lip.
For a while, Sato couldn't say anything.
He didn't understand why she would suddenly say something like that.
But he was really happy.
After all, he'd had feelings for Hirai too.
"Hirai, do you mean it?
If you do, then please give up the black magic.
Even if you don't rely on something like that, I..."
"Huh? What, Sato...?
You what?"
"Like I said, even if you don't rely on black magic..."
"........."{p}
rows.41:a518:
Hirai's feelings were mixed.
After all, she had been using black magic to cast a charm to win his heart.
"...Don't say that.
Sato, please don't say that..."
Tears started dripping down her face.
Seeing that, it clicked for Sato.
She must have gone and done the black magic.
"Hirai, don't tell me..."
He glared at her with accusing eyes.
She couldn't bear it, and just clung to his arm.
"Hirai, let go of me."
He said it coldly.
"So what was the result? Did it say you and I would work out?"
And he pressed her for an answer.{p}
rows.41:a76c:
"Sato, stop..."
She was crying, her nose bright red.
Sato thought it over.
She'd done her fortune, then called him out like this and confessed, so she must have gotten a good result.
It was true that Sato liked Hirai.
But he didn't want her thinking the black magic fortune had come true.
So he decided to be cold to her.
"...I'm sorry.
I just can't return your feelings right now, Hirai..."
Hirai was hurt.{p}
rows.41:a930:
She had done the black magic.
She had even offered up her own cat's blood.
She had thought it would work...
She sank to the ground right there and burst into tears.
And then...{p}
rows.41:a9e4:
"Aaaaaaagh!☆"
Sato clutched his head and began writhing in agony.
She had no idea what was happening, and for a while she just stood there, stunned.
But when she saw him fall to the ground, she rushed straight over.
"Sato...!"
Then Sato, who had been writhing in pain, slowly opened his eyes...
and smiled at Hirai.
"Hirai... I loved you too..."
They say his eyes had gone hollow, as if his soul had been torn out.{p}
rows.41:ab9c:
...Hey, {a}.
There are all kinds of fortune-telling in the world, right?
And after a reading, they sometimes give you some kind of advice, right?
But...
You mustn't swallow all of it whole.{p}
rows.41:ac60:
...Don't you think so?
Some fortunes might hold a terrifying magic power, you know.
Like the black magic Hirai did...
Sato and Hirai got married a few years later, it seems.
So the black magic charm worked just fine.
But...
They say Sato's eyes have stayed hollow ever since.
He even gave up the fortune-telling he used to be so good at.
It seems there's nothing left of the boy she loved.
Her old friends all say the same thing to her, apparently:
"Is this the man who understands everything about you?"
Just like that...{p}
rows.41:ae58:
...{a}.
You know what I think?
If Sato had given Hirai a good answer back then, maybe he wouldn't have ended up like his soul was torn out.
I have that feeling.
Hey, don't you think so...?
Well then, on to the next person's story...
Is what I'd like to say, but the seventh one still isn't here, huh.
What should we do?
Hey, {a}...?{p}
rows.41:af84:
Hmm...
So housework comes second.
You're not that picky about personality?
Like, you'd forgive her even if she was selfish?
You know, Hirai, the girl I just told you about, was exactly that kind of person.
She was really pretty, and her hobby was cooking.
She really wanted to get married, so she even went to cooking school and stuff.
She might've been just your type, {a}.{p}
rows.41:b16c:
Hirai was really into fortune-telling.
She was always fussing about stuff like "Today's my lucky day" or "If you're going on a trip, this day is best."
She didn't seem to have any special sixth sense herself, though.
She went to fortune-telling shops a lot, it seems.
Anyway, Hirai's boyfriend was named Tanaka.
He was going out with a girl with really high standards, after all.
So he was super good-looking.
And he was smart and had a great personality, too.
She used to tell her friends all the time, apparently.
That she wanted to marry Tanaka.{p}
rows.41:b3e4:
That shop stood all alone on a narrow lane between abandoned buildings.
Inside a black tent, a woman wearing a black robe over her head was doing readings all by herself.
Hirai asked the fortune-teller.
She said she wanted to know why Tanaka had turned cold on her.
And she was told that he'd gotten a new girlfriend.
On top of that, the new girlfriend was supposed to be really beautiful.{p}
rows.41:b54c:
Hirai was pretty and had a great figure.
She was pretty confident about herself.
So she got a little ticked off.
She started wondering if the girl was prettier than her, and stuff like that.
And then she got it into her head that she'd become prettier than that girl and show him.
I kind of feel like her way of thinking was a little off, though.
Like, do people really go out and break up just because of looks?
But there are people like you, {a}, who put looks first, huh.
Maybe that kind of thing does happen.{p}
rows.41:b718:
So then, seeing Hirai's attitude, the fortune-teller said something like this.
Shall I teach you how to become even more beautiful?
To become beautiful, it isn't enough to just polish your looks, she said.
Do you get what that means?
It means you have to have allure.
There are all kinds of allure, right?
Besides inner things like being kind or being thoughtful.
There's the air a person gives off... their smile, their cheerfulness.
The individuality that seeps out from their personality, I guess.
Or a sexiness that makes you wonder if they're giving off pheromones.
Do you know what pheromones are?
They're scents that attract the opposite sex.
They're substances that animals give off from their bodies when they want to attract the opposite sex.
With people, that kind of allure apparently isn't something you can just put on because you want to.
But the fortune-teller said this.
That with some method of gathering spiritual power, you could gain an allure so strong it practically gives off a scent.
Hirai said she absolutely wanted to try that method.
And so...{p}
rows.41:badc:
The fortune-teller told her to provide materials for the spell.
First, her hair.
A handful of it.
She had a bit of her hair cut off.
The fortune-teller brought out a knife and hacked it off with one chop.
It made a snapping, tearing sound.
As she listened to that sound with her eyes shut, an image came into her head.{p}
rows.41:bbf0:
An image of a bundle of nerves being snapped apart, strand by strand.
There are no nerves in hair, yet somehow she felt something like pain, like anguish.
Maybe that was the pain in her heart.
And then, the night passed...{p}
rows.41:bcd8:
The next morning, when she looked in the mirror, she felt like she had changed a little somehow.
Her face seemed a bit slimmer.
The expectation that came from having the fortune-teller cast a charm on her.
That was what changed her mood.
So even though she'd been so down the day before, she felt bright and cheerful somehow.{p}
rows.41:bdfc:
She had a fun day.
Hirai was in a different class from Tanaka.
But she went out of her way to borrow a textbook from a friend in Tanaka's class, and stuff like that.
And then it felt like Tanaka was looking at her, now that she'd gotten prettier.
She basked in a feeling of superiority, all by herself.{p}
rows.41:bf30:
...But by after school, that feeling was blown away.
Because Hirai saw it.
On her way home, she saw Tanaka walking with a beautiful woman.
The woman was in regular clothes.
So she didn't seem to be from the same school.
Hirai panicked.
She figured that must be Tanaka's new girlfriend.{p}
rows.41:c068:
So she went to the fortune-teller again.
"Ah, it seems the charm has taken effect."
The fortune-teller greeted her with a smirk.
And then she praised Hirai.
The hem of her black robe swaying as she did.
You really are beautiful, she said.{p}
rows.41:c16c: But Hirai's heart still wasn't satisfied.{p}So what do you think she said?
rows.41:c1dc: I want to curse Tanaka's new girlfriend
rows.41:c1fc:
That's right.
That's what she said.
That she wanted to be made even more, more beautiful.
Then this time, the fortune-teller asked for her nails.{p}
rows.41:c280:
She told Hirai to clip her nails a little and give them to her.
Hirai had the fortune-teller clip her nails.
It was a strange feeling.
Like she was doing something secret...
Well, it really was something secret.
On her way home from the fortune-telling parlor, she kept her head down the whole time.
Giving up her hair and nails to become beautiful...
It seemed so strange to her that she was doing a ritual like that.
What on earth am I doing? she wondered.{p}
rows.41:c40c:
That night, she cried in bed.
She felt so sad she couldn't stand it.
Was she sad because she'd seen Tanaka's girlfriend?
Or because she was ashamed of herself for relying on the power of a charm?
...Either way, she just kept crying, all alone.{p}
rows.41:c510:
And the next day.
The very first thing she did was look in the mirror.
She'd cried all night, so she figured her face had to look awful.
But then...
In the mirror was herself, prettier than yesterday.
Her eyelids weren't puffy in the slightest.
Big round eyes, with curling lashes.
Her skin looked fairer than the day before, too.
She was more impressed with that fortune-teller than ever.
She didn't have room to think that something was strange.
And she thought this.
I want to be even more, more beautiful.{p}
rows.41:c6f0:
And so, that night, when she went to the fortune-teller...
There in the room, she saw someone from behind who looked like Tanaka's current girlfriend.
Hirai panicked.
She thought maybe that girl had gotten this fortune-teller to make her beautiful too.
And that maybe that was how she'd won Tanaka's heart.
Just as Hirai was about to confront her...
"Ugh!☆"
Hirai clutched her chest and collapsed.{p}
rows.41:c870:
Then the woman in front of her rose smoothly to her feet, smiled at Hirai, and said this.
"Tanaka is mine..."
The woman took a black robe out of the desk.
And slowly pulled it on over her head.
What she looked like then...{p}
rows.41:c9dc:
A few days later, a woman's body was found at that fortune-telling parlor, they say.
The body had been dumped in a black garbage bag, together with a doll made of wax.
And inside the wax doll, they say, were the dead woman's hair and nails.
Hey, {a}.
You've heard this story, right?
It was on the news years ago, remember?
That victim was Hirai.
And the cause of death is unknown.
There were no external wounds, and she wasn't sick, either.
.........{p}
rows.41:cb84:
Hey, {a}.
Did you know?
People's hair and nails get used in love charms, like for becoming beautiful or winning someone's heart...
But they say they're also used when you curse someone to death...{p}
rows.41:cc4c:
Oh, right, right.
Tanaka got married, I heard.
The woman he married is supposed to be really beautiful.
Her name is Miwako, apparently.
And after Tanaka got married, someone asked him about Hirai, and this is the answer they got.{p}
rows.41:cd30:
"Hirai?
...Yeah, we did go out for a while.
Back then, she was really into fortune-telling.
Seems she was hanging around some weird shop, too.
Truth is, we didn't go out for very long.
Partly 'cause I met Miwako around then.
Plus, Hirai had this vibe where you couldn't really get close to her, you know?
...And then that whole thing happened, right?
Man, it really wrecked me.
If I hadn't had Miwako back then...
I wonder what would've happened to me."{p}
rows.41:cef4:
...Hey, {a}.
I wonder what really would've happened if this Miwako hadn't been around.
I heard something, you know.
When my big sister went to Tanaka's house to bring him a keepsake of Hirai's...
Miwako was in the Western-style room, wearing a black robe and muttering something.
In front of a photo of Tanaka.
My sister was startled, and Miwako took off the robe right away, apparently...
I wonder what that means.
.........{p}
rows.41:d094:
That's the end of my story.
.........
But.........
The seventh person isn't coming, huh.
What do you want to do?
{a}, should we head home soon...?{p}
rows.41:d110:
This is what she said.
That she wanted to curse Tanaka's new girlfriend.{p}
rows.41:d15c:
Then the fortune-teller fell silent.
With her head still down, she said this to Hirai.
She said...{p}What do you think she said?
rows.41:d1d8: You should work on improving yourself more
rows.41:d1f4: If you're prepared to have no regrets, I'll teach you how to curse
rows.41:d22c:
"A curse won't work unless you cast it yourself.
If you're prepared to have no regrets, I'll teach you how to curse."
That's what she said.
Hirai hesitated a little.
Asking someone else to do it and doing it yourself take different levels of resolve.
But in the end, her wish to get Tanaka back was stronger.
"I'm prepared."
Hirai answered in a trembling voice.
The fortune-teller smiled sweetly, told her to come back at four tomorrow afternoon since she'd prepare the ritual, and closed up the tent.{p}
rows.41:d410:
After practically being chased out of the tent, Hirai felt torn the whole time.
What would a curse involve?
What would happen to the girl once she was cursed?
All kinds of thoughts swirled around in her head.
After a sleepless night...{p}
rows.41:d50c:
Even when morning came, the guilt wouldn't leave Hirai's heart, and that day she couldn't even look Tanaka in the face.
The appointed time was drawing near.{p}What should I do...?
rows.41:d5d0:
I'll go.
I promised, after all, so I have to go.
Hirai made up her mind.
Partly it was because she'd promised, but she also had a feeling that if she didn't go, this time she would be the one cursed.{p}
rows.41:d690:
The fortune-teller was waiting for Hirai in front of the tent.
"Ah, so you kept your promise.
Don't worry, the ritual is all prepared."
With that, the fortune-teller invited her into the tent.{p}
rows.41:d758:
The tent was filled with a horrible stench, and dark red stains were splattered here and there. It felt even more sinister than usual.
"You mustn't touch those stains.
They're no ordinary stains."
Looking closely, the stains seemed to have been made according to some kind of rule.
It's like a magic circle, or a mandala... Hirai thought.
She'd only ever seen either one in books, but the dark red stains really did seem to be drawing a magical barrier.
"Now, please step into the center of the circle, without treading on the lines."
As the fortune-teller urged, Hirai went and stood in the middle of the circle.{p}
rows.41:d964:
Then the fortune-teller handed her a knife.
"This knife has a special cursing power laid upon it.
Now, use it... your blood!"
"Wha-what?!★"
Hirai was shocked.
She'd heard that black magic and such called for the blood of a sacrifice, but she'd never dreamed she would actually go through it herself.{p}
rows.41:da88:
"Well, what's the matter?
Have you gotten scared?"
The fortune-teller watched Hirai with a smirk.{p}Under the gaze of those eyes, Hirai...?
rows.41:db14: Said she was scared and wanted to stop
rows.41:db30: Said she wasn't scared and would go on
rows.41:db58:
Maybe she couldn't give up on Tanaka after all, or maybe the fortune-teller's smile looked like a challenge, but Hirai answered firmly.
"I'm not scared.
Let's continue."
That's what she said.
"My apologies.
Of course you're not.
It's only a matter of letting two or three drops of blood fall from your little finger, after all."
The fortune-teller was still smirking.
But when Hirai heard just two or three drops, she was secretly relieved.
That much, she could just think of as a little cut...
And so, gripping the knife in a hand that still trembled, she cut the very tip of her left little finger, just a tiny bit.{p}
rows.41:de60:
The smoke had a peculiar scent, a little like incense, and wrapped in it, Hirai lost consciousness, they say.
When she came to...{p}
rows.41:defc:
The fortune-teller was nowhere in the tent; instead, an old woman was standing there.
Her head was still spinning.
Was it because of that smoke?
"Um, excuse me.
Where's the fortune-teller who was here?"
"Who knows...
The fortune-teller? Isn't that you, dearie?"
"No way, I'm just a..."
Hirai got that far, then lost her words.
She hadn't noticed before, but she'd passed out sitting in a chair.
The very spot where that fortune-teller always sat.
I thought I collapsed on the floor...?{p}
